scope: Independent visual review of the four assigned Scribe landscape reference pairs only.

method.candidate_scale: 1240x930 native logical pixels at scale factor 1
method.reference_scale: 2480x1860 physical pixels, compared at the equivalent logical scale of 1240x930
method.hash_method: PowerShell Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 on each unmodified PNG file
method.identity_check: All four case_metadata records match the assigned round, run_id, binary_sha256, source_sha256, Scribe profile, reader route, and landscape geometry. Each candidate and reference PNG byte hash independently matches its corresponding case_metadata record.
method.reference_set_identity: The reference-set digest is recorded from the assignment; the individual assigned reference PNG hashes were independently checked.

observations: The open reader retains the integrated header, range progress, chapter navigation, and five-tool strip. The panel content follows the 120-logical-pixel inset and the two page allocations remain visually balanced.
Frontlight and warmth each have a visible value, rail, thumb, and endpoint icons. Candidate values 12 and 8 agree with the recorded preferences; the declared desktop profile exposes both controls.
The automatic-brightness row present in the reference is absent. This is consistent with the task's sensor capability boundary, and the shorter sheet is explained by that removed row.
The header, panel title, values, controls, and progress text remain legible in grayscale. No overlapping or clipped interface text was observed.
intentional_differences: Automatic sensor controls are hidden where physical sensor support is unavailable; the orientation action truthfully describes manual direction.
Desktop captures expose declared profile lighting controls without qualifying physical light effects.
Saved lighting values and source artwork differ from the reference; these differences do not establish a viewport-inset defect.

observations: All four direction cards are visible in one row: right-to-left, left-to-right, vertical page turns, and continuous vertical scrolling. The right-to-left card is visibly selected and matches the recorded direction.
The crop-borders toggle is visible in the left half below the cards and agrees with the enabled recorded preference.
The right half below the cards is empty where the reference exposes the independent cross-page-image splitting toggle. This omission is recorded as P3R1-REF21-1.
The right side of the panel title row lacks the reference's current-book default-direction hint. This information loss is recorded as P3R1-REF21-2.
The cards, crop label, progress section, and tool strip fit within the viewport with readable grayscale contrast and no observed text clipping.
intentional_differences: The manual-orientation header label is consistent with the unavailable hardware sensor boundary.
Source artwork differences are not used to infer a reader viewport defect.

observations: The More sheet is anchored above the shared reader progress section, and the More tool is visibly active.
The retained show-tap-zones toggle and immediate full-refresh action are both fully visible, aligned to the 120-logical-pixel content inset, and readable.
Removing the legacy footer-preference group leaves a compact two-column row. Its resulting sheet-height difference is consistent with the explicit closed-reader override.
No clipped action, overlapping label, or unreadable grayscale state was observed in the retained visible controls.
intentional_differences: The legacy footer display preferences are removed so they cannot restore closed-reader labels, ribbon, notifications, or an invisible footer-cycle hit region.
The remaining actions are reflowed after that removal; exact reference sheet height is not required.
The manual-orientation header label reflects the declared hardware capability boundary.

observations: Chapter and bookmark tabs are visible, with the chapter tab selected. The header's table-of-contents action also has an active indicator.
The chapter list preserves two columns of three rows at approximately 50 logical pixels per row. Titles, dotted leaders, dividers, and the selected-tab underline remain legible without clipping.
The candidate shows chapters 86 through 81 and a first-of-15 folio with a next-page action. This agrees with the recorded 86-chapter data and six rows per folio.
The additional folio row explains the taller sheet and higher sheet top. The shared progress section and 76-logical-pixel tool strip remain fully visible.
The current chapter is 34 and is outside this displayed folio. The absence of a current-chapter dot or progress value on these six unrelated rows is not treated as proof that the marker is missing.
intentional_differences: Real chapter count, chapter titles, download/read state, and displayed folio content may differ from the reference.
Dynamic pagination may increase sheet height; a changed sheet top alone is not a layout defect.
The manual-orientation header label reflects the declared hardware capability boundary.

suggestions.description: The Scribe landscape reading-mode panel omits the independent cross-page-image splitting control.
suggestions.evidence: After normalization to logical scale, the reference contains a labeled splitting toggle in the right half below the four direction cards, approximately x644-1120 and y657-719. The same candidate region is blank while the left crop-borders toggle remains visible. The assigned expected state explicitly requires crop and split controls, and this case has no applicable capability exclusion.
suggestions.recommendation: Restore an independently labeled and operable cross-page-image splitting toggle beside crop borders, showing its real current preference and preserving the two-column row.

suggestions.description: The reading-mode title row omits the current-book default-direction hint.
suggestions.evidence: The reference places a subdued current-book default-direction hint at the right of the reading-mode heading, above the direction cards. The corresponding candidate title-row area is empty, although the recorded state has remember_book_direction enabled and right-to-left selected.
suggestions.recommendation: Display the current book's stored default direction in the title row using the reference's subdued supporting-text treatment and the actual stored value.

limitations: This review covers only the four assigned pairs and does not establish that the full round is clean.
Only existing JSON and unmodified PNG evidence were read. No application, build, test, smoke check, or runtime probe was executed, and no product file was changed.
Static screenshots establish visible fit and contrast but cannot prove hit-target operation, preference persistence, slider bounds, navigation behavior, or physical lighting effects.

The current chapter and known read/download examples are not on the captured first table-of-contents folio, so their dot, progress, read-state, and download-state rendering cannot be independently verified from this assigned screenshot.
All assigned cases have the reader menu open. The pure-artwork closed-reader override and the absence of an invisible footer-cycle hit region are not directly exercised by these images.
Binary and source identities were matched to the case_metadata records rather than recomputed from executable or source files.
